title: ZipVoice long listening heats Xiaomi phones and drains battery quickly
symptom: The user reported fast heating and battery drain on Xiaomi 17 Pro at 1.45x with the screen on and no charging. A controlled 20-minute screen-on, unplugged 1.45x baseline on Xiaomi 15 Ultra also produced clear heating confirmed by the user's touch, substantial charge-counter loss and a supply gap. Subsequent hot-state 2x audio had repeated pauses. The two devices must not be treated as interchangeable acceptance evidence.
root_cause: Not fully established. A bounded simpleperf sample placed over 98% of sampled user-mode CPU in libonnxruntime.so. Subsequent real-device ORT profiling placed 94.8% of recorded model_run wall-clock duration in the four-step Decoder, prioritizing that stage for investigation. This is not a CPU or energy share; profiling overhead was not independently measured, and necessary computation versus synchronization or spinning remains incompletely separated. App-level investigation found bounded preparation and no sustained new generation after pause/stop settled. None of these observations proves that all native work is necessary or that spinning causes the heating.
fix: No accepted thermal fix yet. Candidate C (three threads, original model/voice/four steps) failed the 15 Ultra 20-minute 1.45x comparison: battery ended at 43.3C versus 42.7C, last-five-minute skin mean 46.228C versus 45.853C, and charge loss 451mAh versus 456mAh. The 5mAh difference is below observed counter-update variation, so no energy saving is established. Actual audio also confirmed supply gaps. Restore four threads; do not repeat C long tests on the favorable emulator signal.

The user now explicitly permits 2x to remain temporarily unsupported and sets 1.45x as the primary acceptance speed. The previously frozen temperature and charge-loss criteria are unchanged. Any benefit confined to particular speeds must be reported with that range, not promoted as an improvement across all speeds. Follow the linked plan for conditions, tolerances and results instead of deriving acceptance from thread count, instantaneous CPU or single-segment latency.

Candidate D (four threads, three steps, full reference) now has one 20-minute 15 Ultra comparison with temperature readings meeting the frozen numerical targets, but the required repeat and 15% charge-loss improvement remain unproven. The phone retains D as a provisional candidate. The fresh settings/reading/listening backup taken at this window's start was restored and hash-verified; display settings were restored, playback stopped, wireless ADB disabled, and the phone returned. Further phone work requires an agreed window and a new backup; never restore old window data over subsequent user progress.
evidence: Conditions, original APK identity, sensor distinctions, the baseline table, frozen acceptance criteria, candidate decisions and primary-source comparisons are maintained in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-23-offline-listening-thermal.md.

Actual cold and hot 35-second recordings were independently transcribed and checked against source text without whole-sentence omission or repetition; proper-name homophones do not establish a speech defect. This bounded result does not establish arbitrary-text correctness.

Three valid real-device ORT profiles identify Encoder, Decoder and Vocos by model node prefixes. The 46.037s sum of model_run wall time comprises Encoder 0.315s, Decoder 43.643s and Vocos ONNX 2.080s. All 14 app synthesis starts aligned to one native block each: one Encoder Run, four Decoder Runs and one Vocos Run. This bounded result excludes reference preprocessing, Run-external vector updates, native IStft and application queue gaps, and does not quantify CPU or energy shares.

The profile window logged 13 app synthesis completions for 14 starts. The final in-flight native block finished its Vocos ONNX Run approximately 2.044s after the stop marker; no sustained new generation was observed. This cancellation tail is not proof that audio continued playing or progress was committed after stop.

Candidate C on Xiaomi 15 Ultra produced supply silences of approximately 1.13s, 2.34s and 1.16s in an approximately 105-second actual 2x recording. This establishes a supply problem in that 2x sample, not a 1.45x long-listening failure or a temperature/energy conclusion.

Legado and wallabag use external Android TTS engines or HTTP audio rather than this app's bundled voice-cloning path. Their bounded queues, stale-callback rejection and audio reuse inform mechanisms, not a comparable power claim. Subsequent desktop tests found genuine short-tail savings too infrequent to support the main target; shorter-reference timing remained outside the preset criterion after one calibration; genuine 65-character native merging saved about 14.3% cumulative CPU but adds playback and pause-boundary risks. None became a product change.

C started at battery 33.3C/63% versus baseline 31.6C/45%. Before measurement, the user explicitly requested proceeding with actual starting conditions rather than waiting for an exact temperature. The original thermal/charge improvement targets remain unchanged; initial-state and unmeasured room-temperature differences limit causal attribution. The comparison showed no acceptable thermal benefit, rather than proving three threads are universally worse.

C 1.45x recording contained 24 internal silences of at least 0.6s, totaling 32.060s, excluding startup and deliberate pause. The longest 2.716s and final 1.185s internal silence were independently aligned to finished playback waiting for unfinished generation. These establish at least two supply gaps; the other 22 intervals were not individually attributed.

All 266 matched completed source segments took longer in C: cumulative synthesis 891.752s to 1129.604s, natural audio 1671.066s to 1670.059s. Matched last-five-minute playback-budget/generation ratio dropped from 1.168 to 0.922. This is real-device supply evidence, not an energy conversion or a claim that every difference was caused solely by thread count.

A later desktop four-step/three-step ABBA trial retained four threads and the full reference: same-text cumulative CPU 47.061s to 35.205s, final audio 39.732s to 39.893s. Three steps are below the official documented minimum configuration of four. The user heard the comparison and accepted the samples as broadly comparable, authorizing continued validation of candidate D: four threads, three steps, full reference. This approval covers the short desktop samples only. D passed three existing emulator listening-control tests plus the existing 1.45x actual-output test. Continuous phone output evidence was subsequently obtained with restored scrcpy 4.1; the emulator WAV backend's missing idle-time limitation does not apply to that phone recording.

D's first 20-minute phone run at 1.45x, screen on and unplugged ended at BatteryService 40.4C (current HAL battery 40.9C), versus baseline BatteryService 42.7C. Last-five-minute skin mean was 43.341C versus 45.853C. D started at 33.9C/51% versus baseline 31.6C/45%; room temperature was not independently measured. The user reported warmth clearly reduced from the earlier hot feeling. These observations meet the first run's numerical temperature thresholds, not the required repeat or all-device acceptance.

D's charge counter read 2583 to 2234mAh during the formal window (apparent loss 349mAh), with no update in its final two minutes. About one minute after pausing it updated to 2188mAh (cumulative loss 395mAh). The added 46mAh and idle tail prevent an exact equal-window energy claim: neither approximately 23% saving from 349mAh nor approximately 13.4% from 395mAh is established. The frozen loss threshold of 387.6mAh remains unproven; do not subtract assumed idle consumption or change the target.

The full D phone recording contained no internal silence of at least 0.6s from first output to deliberate pause, with first output approximately 5s. The final-five-minute aggregate playback-budget/generation ratio was 1.550. Pause and stop CPU snapshots were 0%, the service disappeared after stop, and a separate 12-second hot screen-off recording continued audibly. This supports continuity and the checked controls, not word-by-word correctness, arbitrary-text voice quality, overnight background playback or thermal 2x performance.

After the user explicitly allowed mild quality tradeoffs, a bounded desktop 3/2/2/3-step trial on two existing texts retained four threads and the full reference. Cumulative generation CPU decreased from 25.572s to 17.173s (32.85%); each text's final audio duration stayed identical, totaling 27.371s per setting. First-round 1.45x audio samples were presented for user judgment. No two-step product change or phone test has occurred; equal lengths do not establish speech completeness, and desktop CPU is not an energy claim.
failed_attempts: Completely disabling intra/inter-op spinning is not the preferred candidate: emulator audio contained a 1.886-second supply gap, while the matched original APK also paused for 0.909 and 3.333 seconds and had a 6954ms generation outlier. These samples expose supply risk and environmental variation, not proof that disabling spinning caused a performance regression or improved energy use. Do not select this configuration from either isolated sample.

Session force_spinning_stop also failed to show a stable CPU saving across the two matched screening rounds. Do not promote it to a real-device thermal candidate using only the favorable round; the numerical comparison remains in the linked plan.

Combining the same 34-character and 36-character text into one 70-character outer request did not reduce cumulative CPU in either micro-sample round and increased first-audio latency. Normal punctuation and min_char_in_sentence=30 were preserved, so the native layer still split that request into 34- and 36-character chunks. The trial did not actually eliminate the native boundary and therefore does not rule out benefits from reducing genuine native short tails. A punctuation-only split tail is not by itself evidence of an additional complete inference pass; verify native execution rather than counting split strings.
impact: Full thermal and battery acceptance remains open. Candidate C is rejected; D has first-run temperature and playback-continuity improvement at 1.45x, with user-confirmed reduced warmth. A valid repeat and reliable proof of the frozen 15% charge-loss improvement remain outstanding. The user permits temporary lack of 2x support. Preserve offline packaging, accepted voice-quality boundaries, actual selected speed and user data; do not turn a candidate result into a resolved claim.
